audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Ziggs ability is named — everything is "his Q bomb", "W-knockback", "minefield", "his ult" — and the level-6 plan hangs entirely on beating an ability whose cooldown is never given.
audit.why: The whole matchup reduces to one timer. Satchel Charge knocks Ziggs himself away, which is the only thing that undoes your engage, and it is 20 seconds at rank 1 falling to 12. "R him before he can W-knockback you out of range" is therefore not a reaction you win — it is a window you wait for. Naming it and pricing it converts the single most repeated instruction on the page from a hope into a count. Bouncing Bomb at 6 down to 4 seconds and Hexplosive Minefield at a flat 16 are the other two, and 16 seconds is a long time to be minefield-free on a wave he wants to zone.
audit.corrected: All five named; Satchel Charge's 20s and the wait-for-it rule written into spikes[2], mid, wants.you[1] and whys[4].
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json (W 20/18/16/14/12 "Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage"; Q 6/5.5/5/4.5/4; E cd 16)

audit.whatIsWrong: The range gap that defines the lane is asserted qualitatively — "out-ranges my Q-shard by a mile" — and no ultimate cooldowns appear anywhere.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb is 850 and Seismic Shard is 625: a 225-unit gap, which is why you cannot trade and why the answer is farming rather than stepping up. And Mega Inferno Bomb is 120/95/70 against Unstoppable Force's 130/115/100, so his ultimate returns first at every rank — by 30 seconds once both are maxed. That reframes the late game the entry calls a coin-flip: you get one flank per two of his siege ults, so the flank has to actually land.
audit.corrected: The 850-versus-625 numbers added to early and whys[0]; the ultimate comparison to late and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late are written in the first person: "his Q bomb out-ranges my Q-shard", "I cannot trade back, I can only walk up and eat it", "my one real window", "my entire job is to flank". Every other matchup on this champion addresses the reader as "you".
audit.why: It reads as someone else's diary rather than advice, and it is the only entry in the slice that does it. The content is mostly sound; the voice is not the one the rest of the page uses, so a reader hits three paragraphs that suddenly stop instructing them.
audit.corrected: early, mid and late rewritten in second person, with the ability names and cooldowns folded in at the same time.
sources: champ-data/content/malphite.js (early, mid, late for malphite vs ziggs)

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Ziggs / Ziggs / Skill / Skill / Ziggs / Skill / Ziggs, giving him Level 6 and the last stage against the page's own text.
audit.why: spikes[2] calls level 6 "your one real kill window" and whys[4] says "Unstoppable Force gives you a real all-in", yet the chart labels that stage Ziggs. whys[6] calls the last stage "a teamfight coin-flip" — a coin-flip is Skill, not his. The opening two stages are correctly his: an 850-range bomb every 6 seconds against a 625-range melee tank is not a lane you contest.
audit.corrected: Ziggs / Ziggs / Skill / Skill / Malphite / Skill / Skill, which matches the prose and the 50.66% over 762 games.

edits.before: Ziggs is a true ranged poker and the early game is his — his Q bomb out-ranges my Q-shard by a mile, so I cannot trade back, I can only walk up and eat it. Let Granite Shield take the bombs and last-hit at max range; do not greed a Q-shard on him because stepping into his bomb arc just feeds him free poke. There is no all-in here pre-6 — he has no melee answer I can punish, just respect the range and farm.
edits.after: Ziggs is a true ranged poker and the early game is his: Bouncing Bomb reaches 850 to Seismic Shard's 625, so there is no trade you can take, only chip you absorb. Let Granite Shield eat the bombs and last-hit at max range. Do not greed a Seismic Shard onto him — stepping into his arc to spend 70 mana on a 625-range poke buys him a free 6-second bomb. There is no pre-6 all-in here. Respect the range and farm to your ultimate.

edits.before: Around 4-5 my W Thunderclap armor and Granite Shield refresh let me farm through his minefield and ignore a lot of the chip. Level 6 is my one real window: Unstoppable Force is unstoppable, so I want to R him from a fog angle or around a wall before he can W-knockback me out of range and reset the gap. Land that R and I knock him up for my E and an empowered W — that is the whole kill. If I miss it, he just kites and pokes again.
edits.after: Around 4-5 Thunderclap's armor and a recharging Granite Shield let you farm through Hexplosive Minefield, a flat 16 seconds at every rank. Level 6 is your one real window, and it is a counting job rather than a reaction: Satchel Charge knocks Ziggs himself out of your engage, and it is 20 seconds at rank 1. Flank from fog inside that gap, knock him up, then Ground Slam and an empowered Thunderclap. Miss it and he kites and pokes again.

edits.before: This becomes a teamfight and siege game, and it stays even because we each own one half of it. Ziggs out-pokes my whole team and his ult deletes a squishy, but my entire job is to flank from fog and R him out of the backline before he casts — one good Unstoppable Force on him swings the fight. He answers by W-knockback resetting my engage and minefield-zoning the choke, so it comes down to whether I get my flank angle or he keeps his spacing.
edits.after: This becomes a teamfight and siege game, and you each own half of it. Ziggs out-pokes your team and Mega Inferno Bomb deletes a squishy from 5000 range — and at 70 seconds late against your R's 100, he sieges twice for every flank you get. So the flank has to land. Take the fog angle, knock him off the backline, and know his answer is Satchel Charge resetting your engage plus a minefield on the choke. Spacing decides it.

notes: Two entries in _missing-interactions.json for this matchup are built on kit flags that contradict Riot's own description, and I wrote nothing from either. (1) "resistances-invalidated — Ziggs bypasses stacking resistances (Satchel Charge)": Satchel Charge is described as magic damage plus a knock-away with no health scaling at all; the percentHealth flag looks derived from the "hexplode vulnerable enemy turrets" clause. (2) "autoreset-burst-tell — Ziggs's combo opens with an auto-attack reset (Short Fuse)": Short Fuse is a periodic empowered basic attack, not a reset, so there is no wind-up tell to teach. Also, the packet flagged "Let Granite Shield" in early as a probable wrong name — false positive, that is Malphite's real passive with a verb in front, and the checker matched on the verb. The first-person voice in early, mid and late was the largest quality problem in this entry and is worth a grep across other champions; it is unlikely to be confined to one matchup.
